{{Short description|Mathematical treatise by the Banū Mūsā}}
{{Use British English|date=March 2023}}
{{Use dmy dates|date=March 2023}}
{{italic title}}
[[File:F. 122r from Kitāb al-mutawassiṭāt.jpg|thumb|A page of the ''Book on the Measurement of Plane and Spherical Figures'', [[Columbia University]], New York]]

The '''''Book on the Measurement of Plane and Spherical Figures''''' ({{langx|ar|كتاب معرفة مساحة الأشكال البسيطة والكريّة|italic=yes}}, {{transliteration|ar|Kitāb maʿrifah masāḥat al-ashkāl al-basīṭah wa-al-kuriyyah}}){{refn|1=The work is also known as the {{transliteration|ar|Kitāb maʿrifaẗ masāḥaẗ al-aškāl al-basīṭaẗ wa-al-kuriyyaẗ}}.<ref name="Kit">{{cite web |title=Kitāb maʿrifah masāḥat al-ashkāl al-basīṭah wa-al-kuriyyah |url=https://ismi.mpiwg-berlin.mpg.de/text/112939 |publisher=[[Islamic Scientific Manuscripts Initiative]] |access-date=13 April 2023}}</ref>|group=note}} was the most important of the works produced by the [[Banū Mūsā]] (three 9th century Persian brothers who worked in Baghdad).{{sfn|al-Dabbagh|1970|p=444}} A [[Latin]] translation by the 12th century Italian [[astrologer]] [[Gerard of Cremona]] was made, entitled {{lang|la|Liber trium fratrum de geometria}} and {{lang|la|Verba filiorum Moysi filii Sekir}}. The original work in Arabic was edited by the Persian [[polymath]] [[Naṣīr al-Dīn al-Ṭūsī]] in the 13th century.<ref name="OCoRob">{{cite web |last1=O'Connor |first1=J.J. |last2=Robertson |first2=E.F. |title=Banu Musa brothers |url=https://mathshistory.st-andrews.ac.uk/Biographies/Banu_Musa/ |website=[[MacTutor History of Mathematics archive|MacTutor]] |publisher=[[University of St Andrews]] |access-date=18 March 2023 |date=1999}}</ref> The original work in Arabic is not extant, but its contents are known from later translations.{{sfn|Pascual|2015|p=117}}

The treatise, which is about [[geometry]], was similar to two books by [[Archimedes]], ''On the measurement of the circle'' and ''On the sphere and the cylinder''.<ref name="OCoRob" /> It was used extensively in the Middle Ages, and was quoted by authors such as [[Thābit ibn Qurra]], [[Ibn al-Haytham]], [[Leonardo Fibonacci]] (in his {{lang|la|Practica geometriae}}), [[Jordanus de Nemore]], and [[Roger Bacon]].{{sfn|Casulleras|2007}} It deals with the geometrical concepts of [[area]] and [[volume]], [[angle trisection]], [[Straightedge and compass construction|construction]], and [[conic section]]s.{{sfn|Papadopoulos|2016|p=5}} It includes [[theorems]] not known to the Greeks.{{sfn|al-Dabbagh|1970|p=445}} 

The book was re-published in Latin with an English translation by the American historian [[Marshall Clagett]], who has also summarized how the work influenced [[mathematician]]s during the [[Middle Ages]].{{sfn|Pingree|1988}}
